instructions.content: Extract, don't invent: base every insight on actual session content
Be specific: reference actual conversations, tools used and decisions made, and ALWAYS name the session when citing evidence
Detect patterns: look for themes across multiple sessions, not isolated observations
Be domain-appropriate: apply the framework matching the session type, falling back to the generic framework only when domain content is ambiguous
Optionally adapt analysis headings when session content does not fit the standard framework questions
Step 1: if a domain is specified, load its domain-{domain}.md framework; if the file is missing, warn the user and fall back to the generic framework rather than aborting
Step 2: run the session filter script; the first line is PERIOD and must be parsed separately from the session paths
Step 3: read session files and extract conversation turns, tools used and git context
Step 4: analyse what patterns were discovered, what decisions were made and why, what worked or failed, and what recurs across sessions
Step 5: generate Start/Stop/Continue recommendations
Step 6: write insights to the domain insights folder under the PERIOD file name
Step 7: report the file path and suggest the collab or aggregate report command

Follow the report structure: Sessions Reviewed, Domain Learnings (What I Learned, What Worked Well, What Didn't Work, Decisions Made, Patterns Emerged), Start/Stop/Continue, Action Items, Metrics Summary
Include a short Sessions Reviewed list at the top of the report so the reader knows what data was used
Do not run the skill against zero session files; no sessions means no domain insights
Use retrospect-collab instead when the focus is on HOW the collaboration worked, not WHAT was learned
NEVER report a learning that is not evidenced in the session
NEVER apply the generic framework to clearly technical sessions
NEVER omit the Patterns Emerged section when reviewing more than two sessions
NEVER hardcode the output path
